# Portable Pump The portable pump is a portable machine that can be used to quickly .
Similarly to [textlink="canisters" link="GasCanisters"], portable pumps can be used to quickly fill a room whenever [textlink="vents" link="AirVent"] are working too slow, or when a [textlink="vent" link="AirVent"] is not present. They can also be used to siphon gases out of a room as well.
The portable pump requires [textlink="power" link="Power"] through a nearby [textlink="LV cable" link="VoltageNetworks"] while anchored to function.
The portable pump can be configured via a GUI to control the direction to pump gas, the target pressure of the output, and to turn the device on and off.
The pump can be anchored to a [textlink="connector" link="GasCanisters"] to supply it with gas or the drain it for further use.
Portable pumps have an internal capacity of [color=orange][protodata="PortablePump" comp="PortablePump" member="Volume"/] liters[/color] and a maximum operational pressure of [color=orange][protodata="PortablePump" comp="PortablePump" member="MaximumPressure"/] kPa.
## Using Air Tanks with the Portable Pump Portable pumps have a slot for air tanks. When an tank is inserted, the portable pump will treat the tank as the exterior, pumping gas in and out of it instead of the environment.
This can be used to fill tanks with higher pressures than can be achieved with a gas canister, or to siphon gases from tanks into a [textlink="pipenet" link="PipeNetworks"].
Caution should be taken when removing a tank from a pump, as the pump will not stop automatically when a tank is removed, and will immediately start pumping gas to or from the environment.
